summary: Write 0.11.0 SRS for four required Core changes (C4 registration list/listener, C6a req.socketAddress, C6b trustProxyHops/Cidrs + accessors, C7 req.requestId) and the full auth/RBAC v1 module (utils.auth in NaruServe-api: tokens, passwords, users/groups/RBAC, transport/CSRF/endpoints, abuse protection, API keys, JDBC reference stores), no new dependencies, Java 8 / API 21.

requirement_inventory.notes: Returns registrations in registration order as records {kind, method, path, target}; read-only view; names are proposals. Replaces the current partial bookkeeping (only routes/ws and the separate use(Middleware) list at DefaultRestApp.java:918/:991/:844/:854).

Kinds: ROUTE, WEBSOCKET, STATIC, ROUTER_MOUNT, GROUP, CORS, MIDDLEWARE, PATH_MIDDLEWARE, ERROR_MIDDLEWARE, PARAM. MIDDLEWARE = use(Middleware) and path-less (`""` or `"/"`) use/useAsync; PATH_MIDDLEWARE = any other path, pattern or array; staticFiles is tagged STATIC and cors is tagged CORS even though they are internally use("")/use(options.middleware()).

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Registration target is the original registered object
requirement_inventory.notes: `target` is the user-registered middleware, Router, or error handler, not a Core-created wrapper; onError wraps the handler in a lambda (DefaultRestApp.java:941-944) so the record must hold the unwrapped handler (13판). Needed so auth can identify its own auth.errors()/errorMiddleware() instance.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Mounted Router and group registrations are expanded with the mount path
requirement_inventory.notes: Routes inside a mounted Router or group are recorded with the mount path prefixed; later additions to an already mounted live Router are also expanded and reported. Registrations that cannot be expanded (regex or array paths) must be identifiable as such for protectOnly checks.

`app.onRegistration(RegistrationListener)` (proposed name) notifies on every later registration, including post-start ones; the listener type must be a @FunctionalInterface so Kotlin lambdas compile. Listener registration is always allowed regardless of auth protectOnly.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Registration ordering contract: validate, listener, apply, record
requirement_inventory.notes: Per registration: Core input validation first, then the listener synchronously BEFORE the registration takes effect, then apply, then record. A listener exception aborts the registration (not applied, not recorded) and propagates to the caller, also through Router. Requires splitting validation out of `http.methods(...)` (DefaultRestApp.java:916-917); fixed by one Core test.

After start only ROUTE, use, mount and param can be registered; cors, ws, staticFiles, group, onError, trustProxy stay rejected by existing requireConfigurable/AppLifecycle guards. The listener is notified for the allowed post-start kinds, including use(ErrorMiddleware) which is still accepted after start.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Registration API docs and Kotlin SAM coverage
requirement_inventory.notes: docs/api entry with Express comparison and Java/Kotlin examples; Kotlin source test compiles `app.onRegistration { r -> }` and reads registrations (T11). Names are proposals; mark as (미확정) then settle during implementation per CLAUDE.md.

Returns the real connection peer address independent of any trustProxy setting and of X-Forwarded-*/Forwarded headers; used for the loopback test in the local-request rule. Nullability and type (String vs InetSocketAddress) are open; choose the one consistent with remoteAddress().

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: socketAddress() supplied by every engine adapter
requirement_inventory.notes: TinyHttpd adapter, in-memory test adapter and Servlet adapter (getRemoteAddr) must supply it; 00 §12 says Servlet container values are unverified, so the Servlet mapping is an explicit test item.

requirement_inventory.area: C6b proxy trust hops and CIDR
requirement_inventory.notes: Resolves X-Forwarded-For from the right: the nth hop from the right is the client address. n >= 1 also means the direct socket peer is trusted. Hop mode requires the node to be reachable only through the LB (document as a mandatory precondition).

requirement_inventory.area: C6b proxy trust hops and CIDR
requirement_inventory.notes: Resolves X-Forwarded-For from the right to the first address outside the trusted CIDRs; the peer is trusted only if the socket address is inside a trusted CIDR. Needs CIDR parsing/validation for IPv4 and IPv6 with bad input rejected.

requirement_inventory.area: C6b proxy trust hops and CIDR
requirement_inventory.notes: XFP is read only when the direct peer is trusted. One XFP value: use it. Several: hop mode takes the nth from the right; CIDR mode takes the value at the same position as the first untrusted XFF entry counted from the right. If XFP has 2+ items and the count differs from XFF or the position is missing, result is false (fail closed). Proxies that pass XFP through without overwriting are unsupported.

requirement_inventory.area: C6b proxy trust hops and CIDR

requirement_inventory.area: C6b proxy trust hops and CIDR

requirement_inventory.notes: Existing leftmost-XFF trustProxy(true) stays for compatibility (FR-ENGINE-008) but docs state the spoofing risk; this is a Core-wide security defect independent of auth. Interaction when legacy and hop/CIDR modes are both set is unspecified: pick last-wins or reject at implementation.

requirement_inventory.area: C6b proxy trust hops and CIDR

requirement_inventory.notes: remoteAddress() returns the resolved client IP and isSecure() honors the resolved XFP only when the peer is trusted; spoofed XFP/XFF from an untrusted peer is ignored. Existing FR-HTTP-011 and FR-ENGINE-008 behavior without trust must stay unchanged.

requirement_inventory.notes: New configuration methods follow the NEW-state guard (IllegalStateException outside NEW), reject hops < 0 / null / malformed CIDR; Kotlin test and docs/api update included.

Publishes the existing package-private DefaultRequest request id (DefaultRequest.java:390). The value must equal the `requestId` in the standard error body and the `rid` of the access log line for the same request (FR-APP-006 / FR-APP-015 AC-7).

Package com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.auth (+ jwt, password, user, group, rbac, audit, apikey, spi, jdbc, testing, internal) in NaruServe-api; no new Gradle module and no new library; mainDependencies unchanged. Subpackage layout and which types are public vs internal are listed in 00 §2 tree.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: utils.auth uses only Core public API
requirement_inventory.notes: No import of com.snoworca.naruserve.internal from utils.auth; enforce with an architecture test. Also no java.nio.file, java.time, CompletableFuture, java.util.function.Function (API 24+), android.*, servlet.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: API 21 and Java 8 conformance of auth classes
requirement_inventory.notes: JDK-only APIs: javax.crypto.Mac, java.security, java.sql/javax.sql.DataSource, java.text.Normalizer, FileDescriptor.sync, java.util.concurrent; animal-sniffer android-api-level-21 must pass (00 §12 says availability was never checked). Interface default methods must work under D8 desugaring.

com.snoworca.naruserve.utils.TimeSource with nowMillis(); replaces java.time (API 26+); all public timestamps are epoch-millisecond long/Long. Used for key expiry, token exp, throttle windows and tests.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Auth.builder(secret) minimal path and secret validation
requirement_inventory.notes: Auth.builder(@Nullable String) = KeySources.of(secret); build() throws AuthConfigException for null, short or example secrets with a message that includes how to generate one (`openssl rand -base64 32`). DEV may generate a temporary key and logs that restart invalidates all tokens.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Builder validation reports all incompatibilities at once
requirement_inventory.notes: build() collects every inconsistent combination into one AuthConfigException; unknown config keys are errors. Includes: MULTI_INSTANCE with in-memory/file stores, invalid scheme names, mountPath '/' in cookie modes, `.permitPrefix("/")`, empty permit path.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: AuthConfig.load(file) with env: and file: secret references
requirement_inventory.notes: Code builder is the single source of truth; AuthConfig.load reads a config file and feeds the builder; secrets referenced as `env:NAME` or `file:/path`; unknown keys rejected. File format is not specified in 00 (04 §1 only).

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: AuthMode DEV and PROD with fromEnv()
requirement_inventory.notes: fromEnv(): NARU_ENV=dev -> DEV, anything else (incl. unset) -> PROD. DEV relaxes only: missing secret -> temp key, R33 secure-transport check off, hash cost/key strength FAIL -> WARN. DEV never relaxes default-deny, install order, public-path rules, CSRF, throttling, grant rules, JSON errors. DEV with non-local request logs one WARN.

Security-level presets selecting default numbers/policies; default profile and the min-password length are an open question to be decided at implementation (07 recommends STANDARD with length 8 vs NIST 15). The exact per-profile values live in the stale 07, not in 00.

Default SINGLE_INSTANCE. MULTI_INSTANCE makes build() fail when any in-memory or file store is present. Heuristic WARNs: shared-less RefreshTokenStore/LoginThrottle with proxy headers seen; refresh with an unknown family on an in-memory store (401 + WARN once). UserStore should give read-after-write `ver` consistency (Javadoc).

Accounts are created in onStart only when absent, never overwritten; hash computed in build(); a concurrent create hitting DuplicateUserException logs INFO 'already exists'. Env var is NARU_ADMIN_PASSWORD. Origin BOOTSTRAP, emits onUserCreated only (no before event). Null-password rule: only one admin-role .user may have null; checked in onStart for missing accounts; violations are doctor FAIL (DEV also FAIL for non-admin null).

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: First-admin setup endpoint and recovery mode
requirement_inventory.notes: POST /auth/setup body {token, username, password}; requires a local request (R33 definition) AND a one-time setup token printed to the log; 404 once an admin exists; reopened only by .recovery(true)/NARU_AUTH_RECOVERY=1; closes after first success in the process; a .user(name,null,...)-opened setup forces username==name else 400 `username_mismatch` and grants that .user's roles. Recovery creates or reactivates+resets password+grants admin with ver++, WARNs on every start, is audited, and rejects service accounts with 400 `service_account_no_password`. No before events; emits on* with Origin SETUP/RECOVERY.

install throws IllegalStateException('auth.install(app) must come before routes; found GET /x registered before it') when C4 holds ROUTE/WEBSOCKET/STATIC/ROUTER_MOUNT/GROUP before it. Path-less middleware kinds (cors, accessLog, use(Middleware), error middleware, param) are allowed and listed by doctor.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Pre-install middleware and CORS ordering doctor rules
requirement_inventory.notes: doctor FAIL (DEV included) for path-scoped use(path|Object, mw)/useAsync(path) before install unless whitelisted with `.allowPreAuthMiddleware(path...)`, and FAIL if cors is registered after install ('cors must be registered before auth.install'). auth does not pass OPTIONS preflight itself; the 4판 'OPTIONS + Access-Control-Request-Method -> next()' rule is withdrawn because Origin-less requests bypassed auth.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: install wiring: middleware, routers and lifecycle hooks
requirement_inventory.notes: app.use(auth) once, using use(Middleware) or use("", mw) so it joins the WebSocket upgrade pipeline (never use(Object, Middleware)); mounts auth.routes() at /auth and auth.adminRoutes() at /auth/admin, each with an auth-specific ErrorMiddleware; onStart runs doctor (any FAIL stops startup) and seeding; onStop stops the cleanup scheduler and flushes files.

`.permit(path)` = exact path, GET and HEAD only; `.permit(Method, path)` opens other methods; `.permitPrefix(path)` matches path or path+'/'; `.permitPrefix("/")` and empty path rejected by build(); ASCII only; compared on the raw undecoded req.path() so /HEALTH, /health/, percent-encoded and non-ASCII variants are NOT public (401). Mismatch with Core routing always errs toward closed.

On a secure transport a valid token attaches a principal; invalid/expired token or multiple credentials yields anonymous (not 401); on plaintext transport the token is not read at all (so LB health checks over HTTP work). Apps read it with auth.userOrNull(req).

Default-deny applies only under the listed ASCII prefixes plus /auth; others are public; shown in describe() and startup log. Range test normalizes more widely than Core: percent-decode, lower-case, merge slashes; any '.' or '..' segment after decoding, or decode failure, counts as protected. doctor FAIL if C4 contains regex/array paths or non-expandable registrations; runtime listener throws IllegalStateException for such later registrations; out-of-scope ROUTE/WEBSOCKET are listed as WARN.

Upgrade detection joins all Connection/Upgrade header lines via req.headers(String) and treats any `upgrade` token in Connection as an upgrade (wider than Core, so h2c upgrades on public paths get 401); independent of permit/protectOnly; only `.permitWebSocket(path)` opens one, compared exactly against the decoded WebSocket req.path().

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: All auth responses are JSON; middleware and router error handling
requirement_inventory.notes: Middleware/guards respond directly and do not call next on failure; store calls inside global middleware and guards are try/caught -> 503 JSON; auth routers carry an ErrorMiddleware mapping HttpException (400/413/415), AuthRejection, other exceptions -> 503 (store) or 500; no stack trace or raw exception messages; body {"error":{"code","message","requestId"}}; AuthResponses user implementations are wrapped and fall back to the default JSON on exception.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: auth.errors() and auth.errorMiddleware() for app handlers
requirement_inventory.notes: auth.errors() is a Core error handler for app.onError placed last; maps DuplicateUserException 409, AuthUnavailableException 503, IllegalArgumentException (auth subclass) 400, AuthRejection (status/code, Retry-After) and AuthStateException (500 without message); other exceptions pass to the next layer. auth.errorMiddleware() does the same via app.use after start. Both return the same instance per Auth.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Error layer placement check at request time
requirement_inventory.notes: On the first request after start (and after listener-flagged post-start registrations) inspect C4: WARN if a ROUTE follows the last auth error layer; WARN at most once per minute; routes added to an already mounted Router count at the mount position. doctor also checks that the very object returned by errors()/errorMiddleware() follows the last ROUTE, not just any error handler.

Unchecked; ctor (int status, String code, @Nullable String message) and 4-arg with @Nullable Long retryAfterSeconds; status must be 4xx; code matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63} else IllegalArgumentException; null message -> default text; getRetryAfterSeconds() produces a Retry-After header in all auth error paths.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Auth status and error code catalog
requirement_inventory.notes: Fixed codes: unauthenticated 401, invalid_token 401, invalid_api_key 401, insufficient_scope 403, api_key_not_allowed 403, insecure_transport 403, csrf_failed 403, api_key_limit 409, too_many_attempts 429, service_account_no_password 400, username_mismatch 400, security_write_conflict 503; Core spellings BAD_REQUEST, NOT_FOUND, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE for input checks, 404, store errors and 415 (thrown as Core HttpException). invalid_request is reserved for the RFC 6750 multiple-credentials 400.

All methods default no-op. Before events: beforeLogin, beforeUserCreate, beforeUserUpdate (old and new values), beforeUserDelete; synchronous, may throw AuthRejection; any other exception (incl. HttpException) is logged and becomes AuthUnavailableException/503. on* events run after the write and failures are only logged. setup, recovery and bootstrap emit on* only.

Table fixes for register, A2, AuthUsers.create/update/rename/delete, bootstrap, setup, recovery, A4 (one before/one on for all changed fields), PATCH /auth/me, POST /auth/password which before/on events fire, with which UserChange values (USERNAME, PASSWORD, ROLES, ENABLED, ATTRIBUTES) and which UserOrigin (REGISTER, ADMIN, APP, SELF, SETUP, RECOVERY, BOOTSTRAP); onPasswordChanged fires whenever a password changes; paths not in the table emit no user events.

@Nullable UserOrigin; non-null only for user-change events (before/on create, update, delete, onPasswordChanged); null for beforeLogin/onLogin/onLogout/onTokenRefreshed/onGroupChanged. Policies should test `== UserOrigin.REGISTER` to restrict only self-registration.

Every AuthUser passed to any AuthEvents callback is a copy with passwordHash null; one event-contract test records every callback over every path and asserts null hash, also covering AuthUsers returns and mutator inputs.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Principal API: AuthPrincipal, user(req), userOrNull, loadUser, authenticated()
requirement_inventory.notes: AuthPrincipal getters never throw (pre-filled by middleware); auth.user(req) throws AuthStateException (IllegalStateException subclass, mapped to message-less 500) when no principal; userOrNull for public paths; loadUser is @Nullable and never throws (store error -> logged, null); authenticated() guard promotes and answers 401/503 JSON on failure.

Route guards usable as the (String, Middleware, RouteHandler) overload and Kotlin trailing lambda; 403 insufficient_scope on missing scope; route(path).use(guard) for RouteGroup which lacks the overload. Guard semantics for roles and wildcard scopes follow R46.

Global middleware only verifies the token and attaches a minimal principal {id}: username '', empty roles/scopes/attributes, isLoaded() false, hasScope false; guards promote via principal cache with ver/enabled checks. Routes without guards skip store lookups and revocation until access TTL; doctor WARN says use only getId() there. Refresh, device tokens, API keys and WebSocket rechecks still revoke immediately.

Per-user cache of user row, expanded groups, roles and scopes for userCacheTtl (default 5 s); ver/enabled mismatch with the token -> 401; auth-originated user changes invalidate that user's entry on that node, group/role changes clear the whole cache; other nodes lag up to the TTL. Authorization decisions (R31) bypass this cache.

Each item reports FAIL or WARN; any FAIL stops start. Items: store connectivity, secret strength, public path list, pre-install middleware list, registration enabled, measured hash cost, clock, proxy trust (R32), deployment vs store (R35), supportsAtomicFieldWrites (R37), supportsAtomicLimitInsert and admin-scope key counts and opt-in warning (R47), usesLimitArguments, null-password .user, file state (R42), cookie WebSocket origin wildcard (R40), errors() placement (R30), WebSocket wrapper count vs WEBSOCKET registrations (R40). DEV turns cost/strength FAIL into WARN.

describe() lists protection scope ('protected: /api, /auth' in protectOnly mode), permitted paths, mode, profile, transport; startup log states restart invalidation for temp keys, that `.user` never overwrites existing passwords, and the allowInsecureTransport reason. Exact format not specified.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Sensitive value hygiene in logs, messages and audit
requirement_inventory.notes: Never log or embed in exceptions/audit events: naru_at, naru_rt, naru_csrf, naru_device values, Authorization values, plaintext API keys or prefix+secret (prefix alone allowed), password characters; char[] buffers wiped after use.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Audit event stream: AuditEvent, AuditSink, AuditSinks
requirement_inventory.notes: Fixed AuditEvent schema with PII minimization; sinks (e.g. logging) in audit package; events required by rules: grant denials, recovery use, security_write_conflict, API key issue/revoke with issuedByUserId and apiKeyId, service-account marker. The schema fields live in stale 07 §6.

tokenFor(auth, name, roles...) works only on InMemoryUserStore (IllegalStateException otherwise; undeclared role -> IllegalArgumentException); tokenForUserId(auth, id) for any store (unknown id -> IllegalArgumentException); apiKeyFor(auth, ownerUserId, scopes...) via the normal issue path; csrfTokenFor(auth, accessToken) (name unconfirmed) builds the CSRF token from the token's sub/fam; verifyUserStore and verifyApiKeyStore contract tests. Tokens issued without a refresh record must still pass CSRF with synthetic fam.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Interface evolution rule for user-implemented SPIs
requirement_inventory.notes: After first public release user-implemented interfaces (UserStore, GroupStore, GroupAdminStore, RoleStore, ApiKeyStore, AuditSink, AuthEvents, PasswordHasher, all spi) only gain default methods; the Forwarding* classes are updated in the same change. The ApiKeyStore and LoginThrottle tables must be fixed before first publication.

If no trust config is set but a request carries X-Forwarded-For, WARN once at runtime ('set trustProxyHops: all users share the LB IP'); MULTI_INSTANCE with no trust config -> doctor WARN; PROD with legacy trustProxy(true) -> doctor FAIL; hop mode under MULTI_INSTANCE or STRICT -> doctor WARN recommending CIDR mode.

Own implementation on javax.crypto.Mac; access claims {sub, ver, fam, iat, exp, jti}, header {alg, typ, kid}; typ `at+jwt` for access and `rt+jwt` for refresh with different derived keys; alg none and unexpected alg rejected; fam = family id of the paired refresh token (new pair -> new fam, rotation keeps fam). v1 tokens carry no scope claim. Public JwtKeys/JwtClaims/JwtException allow standalone use.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: KeySource, KeySources and kid key sets
requirement_inventory.notes: KeySources.of/fromEnv/fromFile/fromBytes/rotating; set = one signing key plus n verification keys addressed by kid; short or example keys refused at build(); purpose-specific derived keys (device `HMAC(secret,'naru-device')`, fingerprint `naru-device-fp`, access/refresh distinct); rotation keeps old tokens valid while the key remains in the verification list.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: MiniJson strict parser with CLAIMS and FILE profiles
requirement_inventory.notes: Internal parser/writer. CLAIMS: depth 2, total 8 KB, string 1 KB; FILE: depth 8, 8 MB default (builder can raise), string 64 KB; both reject duplicate keys, NaN, invalid escapes, trailing characters. JWT header/claims use CLAIMS, auth files use FILE; EXTERNAL_CLAIMS (depth 4, 16 KB) is v2. Files above the cap -> doctor WARN to use JDBC.
Base64url without padding, HMAC signing helpers and constant-time comparison used by JWT, CSRF, device tokens and API key hash comparison; internal and not contract-stable.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: TokenService and TokenPair issue and refresh rotation
requirement_inventory.notes: Issues access+refresh pairs, refresh rotation within the same family, per-family reuse detection (`revokeFamily`, `onRefreshTokenReused`, RFC 9700 4.14); password change returns a fresh pair on a new family. The reuse grace window is an open question to settle at implementation (default 0 s vs a few s).

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: RefreshTokenStore SPI with in-memory, file and JDBC defaults
requirement_inventory.notes: Family and record store: find, markUsed, revokeFamily; default impl follows the user store (InMemory -> memory, File -> same directory file, Jdbc -> JDBC; custom user store without a store -> memory + doctor WARN 'restart logs everyone out'); written only on login/refresh/logout; cleanup by a 10-minute daemon scheduler stopped in onStop. Logout validity check does not trigger reuse detection.
Default hasher is own PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (no external lib); PasswordHasher exposes accepts(hash) prefix routing, verify, hash, needsRehash; hash string format is specified in stale 04 §2.4, not 00.

HashCost.calibrate(ms) targets 250-500 ms within 50,000-600,000 iterations, rounded down to 10,000 steps; HashCost.fixed(n); doctor reports measured cost on this device; re-hash on login only if stored cost < 80% of target, or > 125% of target (needsRehash true). 06's 9-21 s Android numbers are estimates.

chain(new, legacy...) selects by accepts(prefix); legacy: bcrypt ($2a/$2b/$2y accepted, $2x rejected, cost cap 14, concurrency-limited), unsalted MD5/SHA-1/SHA-256, salted SHA-256; successful legacy login re-hashes to PBKDF2 via updatePasswordHash; digest/saltedDigest factory helpers. bcrypt and Blowfish are implemented in-house (04 §2.4.1).

Every hashing operation (login, /auth/password, register, setup, admin create/reset, AuthUsers.create, checkPassword) takes a slot: slots = max(1, cores/2), wait queue 4x slots, wait cap 5 s, beyond that 503 with Retry-After (AuthUnavailableException for app calls); hash endpoints are registered with methodAsync so waiting does not hold worker threads.

Every login attempt runs target-cost PBKDF2 exactly once inside a slot (real verify for PBKDF2 users, legacy verify + dummy PBKDF2 for legacy users, dummy for unknown users); all failure responses (503 included, 429 excluded) are sent after max(1.25T, elapsed) + 0-50 ms jitter using a scheduler, not a blocked thread. Residual risk documented: dormant high-cost bcrypt or over-125% PBKDF2 accounts are distinguishable.

After login success the rehash is queued outside the slot: max 100 entries (overflow dropped and retried at next login), one daemon worker that takes a free slot before hashing; queued plaintext kept as char[] and wiped immediately after use.

PasswordPolicy (min length etc.) applied to register, setup, create, password change, reset; BreachedPasswordChecker is an SPI hook. No rule details in 00; the default length is an open question settled at implementation.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Authenticator SPI with password, Bearer and API key authenticators
requirement_inventory.notes: SPI for credential verification; built-ins for password, Bearer JWT and API key (apiKey is the 'ApiKey' scheme path in R47). Method shapes are in stale 05 §5.

In PROD, authenticated requests and credential endpoints are served only if (a) req.isSecure() is true (direct TLS or XFP https from a C6b-trusted proxy) or (b) the request is local: req.socketAddress() is loopback and no X-Forwarded-*/Forwarded header exists; otherwise 403 insecure_transport and the token is not read. This check is first, before reading any credential. Public paths are exempt (anonymous, token unread).

Disables the secure-transport check but forces access TTL 5 min, refresh TTL 24 h, a warning when cookies lack Secure, and a startup WARN with the reason every boot. DEV disables the check without the opt-in.

Eight credential endpoints: five anonymous-entry (login, refresh, logout, register, setup) and three subject-required (POST /auth/password, POST /auth/me/apikeys, POST /auth/admin/apikeys); independent of .permit; the first group ignores invalid/expired JWT and cookie access tokens as anonymous, the second answers 401 invalid_token with WWW-Authenticate Bearer error="invalid_token".

HEADER reads only Authorization Bearer; COOKIE reads only naru_at; BOTH reads both and treats co-presence as multiple credentials; unread credentials are treated as absent; API key scheme header is read in every mode; multiple Authorization headers -> 400 invalid_request regardless of mode; multiple naru_at -> 400 on protected and subject-required endpoints, ignored on anonymous-entry and public paths.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Request decision order for auth endpoints
requirement_inventory.notes: Order: R33 transport -> multiple credentials / API-key procedure -> body format (415) -> COOKIE-mode body refreshToken (400 BAD_REQUEST) -> CSRF/Origin (403) -> handler; API key requests use the longer eleven-step chain of R47.

401 carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` (with `error="invalid_token"` only for invalid JWT); with API keys enabled one header lists both challenges joined by a comma (`Bearer, ApiKey`, `Bearer error="invalid_token", ApiKey`); no error attribute on the key challenge; 403 for key-authenticated requests carries no WWW-Authenticate at all; 403 insufficient_scope on JWT requests carries Bearer error attribute.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: JSON-only POST bodies on auth endpoints
requirement_inventory.notes: A request with a body (Content-Length > 0 or Transfer-Encoding) whose Content-Type fails Core's JSON test gets 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, including logout that ignores its body; bodiless refresh (cookie) and logout skip the check. Blocks form-encodable CSRF without preflight.

COOKIE-origin writes need header X-CSRF-Token equal (constant time) to cookie naru_csrf and the HMAC (`sub.fam.random16`) bound to the sub and fam of the presented access/refresh token; duplicate naru_csrf cookies pass if at least one equals the header and has a valid HMAC for this request's sub/fam, else 403 csrf_failed; the token is regenerated for the new family on every token-issuing response.

Cookie-planting responses (Set-Cookie of naru_at/rt/csrf/device) always require an Origin check regardless of token source (prevents login CSRF with an attacker refresh token); Origin missing with no Referer, or `Origin: null`, -> 403 csrf_failed in COOKIE mode; trustedOrigins list; SameSite=Strict cookies; login/register/setup check Origin only.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: CSRF for anonymous-entry endpoints refresh and logout
requirement_inventory.notes: refresh with naru_rt cookie: verify the refresh token first, then header==cookie and HMAC vs the refresh token's sub/fam, all before rotation, regardless of access cookie state; body refreshToken (HEADER/BOTH only) skips CSRF and returns body-only without cookies; COOKIE mode body refreshToken -> 400 BAD_REQUEST; logout applies the same checks using the chosen identity token, except body-token and Bearer identities.

Five token-issuing responses (login, register, setup, refresh, password): HEADER always body (accessToken, refreshToken, deviceToken); COOKIE always cookies (naru_at, naru_rt, naru_csrf, naru_device) plus body csrfToken only. BOTH: refresh and password follow how the credential arrived (body refresh token wins over cookie; Bearer -> body, naru_at -> cookie); login/register/setup use Origin then Referer: same-origin or trustedOrigins -> cookies, otherwise body and no Set-Cookie (no 403). Origin-less clients behave like HEADER.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Cookie attributes, paths and clearing rules
requirement_inventory.notes: Cookies naru_at, naru_rt, naru_csrf, naru_device; naru_rt Path = mount (default /auth) so logout receives it; naru_rt not read on other paths; mountPath '/' in cookie modes -> AuthConfigException; multiple naru_rt -> treated as absent; clear with the same Path and Domain as set; HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict defaults via .cookies(); changing Path/Domain in a deployment needs app-side expiry of old cookies (documented, not detectable).

Docs: allowedHeaders must include Authorization, Content-Type, X-CSRF-Token and Naru-Device when sent; BOTH-mode body clients (Capacitor, other-site SPA) go in allowedOrigins but not trustedOrigins; SameSite=Strict cookies do not travel cross-site.

Credentials from JSON body, normalized username; passes beforeLogin, throttle, device trust, constant-work hash; returns token pair per delivery rules plus device token when issued; async handler; anonymous-entry classification; service account with password -> same 401 and timing as wrong password.

Refresh token from body (HEADER/BOTH) or naru_rt (COOKIE/BOTH); rotation with same family; reuse of a used token revokes the family; API key header present -> 403 api_key_not_allowed before reading the refresh cookie.

Anonymous-entry but identity is derived: decision table 1) body refreshToken (HEADER/BOTH): valid -> revoke its family F, and in BOTH also a valid same-sub naru_rt family G (no CSRF/Origin for either); invalid body token -> no identity; 2) no body token and one naru_rt: valid -> identity with CSRF+Origin (403 otherwise, nothing revoked); 3) no refresh token: valid Bearer (no CSRF) or naru_at (CSRF+Origin); 4) no identity: plain logout 204 clearing cookies, ?all=true -> 401 invalid_token (tokens present but invalid) or unauthenticated (no tokens). Store errors -> 503. ?all=true = ver++; without RefreshTokenStore plain logout also ver++. Refresh-token validity checks RefreshTokenStore state without triggering reuse detection.

GET returns the principal's public profile (no hash); PATCH changes only attributes listed in `allowedAttributes`, raises beforeUserUpdate (origin SELF); both need JWT auth, PATCH is forbidden for API keys (403 api_key_not_allowed), GET allowed. No email-change endpoint in v1.

Verifies current password (per-user-id limit 15 min / 5, 429), then changePassword(id, oldHash, tokenVer, newHash) as atomic hash swap + ver++; mismatched ver or disabled -> 401; on race re-verifies the current password against the newly read hash and retries once, otherwise 409; returns a new token pair on a new family, new device token and CSRF token per delivery rules; emits beforeUserUpdate/onUserUpdated/onPasswordChanged.
Self-registration, off unless `.register(true)`; beforeUserCreate with Origin REGISTER; hashes through the slot; named `register` not `signup`; DuplicateUserException -> 409.

15 admin endpoints (A1-A6 users, G1-G8 groups, DELETE users/:id/lockout) under /auth/admin; reads need auth-users:read / auth-groups:read, writes the :write scope and then R31; G9 group-role assignment is v2 and absent. The exact route/body table is in stale 05 §4.2 and R45 says the SRS must fix it as a table.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Admin PATCH A4 application order and applied list
requirement_inventory.notes: R31 checked once over all changed fields; apply order username -> password -> other security fields -> profile; username conflict -> 409 with applied: []; same-as-current username is a no-op; password race -> 409 with applied only containing an earlier rename; later failure -> 503 with the applied list and audit event; one onUserUpdated for what was applied; admin username change goes through the rename path.

Auth and Origin are decided before the 101 (Origin by Core WebSocketUpgrade, default same-origin; cookie mode with wildcard allowed origins -> doctor FAIL, WARN if unreadable); wrapper schedules close(1008, 'token expired') at access exp, rechecks principal every userCacheTtl, closes on auth-triggered revocations immediately on that node; API-key connections close at key expiresAt ('api key expired') and on key deletion/staleness/invariant violation/pending marker; doctor WARN if WEBSOCKET registrations exceed wrapper uses.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Login throttling keys, limits and enumeration resistance
requirement_inventory.notes: Three keys on normalized username (counted even for unknown names so 429 never reveals an account): (user, IP) 5 per 15 min, IP 20 per 15 min (exempt for trusted devices), user-only 10 per 15 min (only for non-trusted-device requests); numbers configurable; exceeding -> 429 too_many_attempts with Retry-After, never sleeping; IP is R32-resolved, IPv6 grouped by /64.

1) device token passing HMAC/expiry and fingerprint -> defer IP key, otherwise check IP key first; 2) (user, IP) key always; 3) findByUsername and user id/ver match confirm trust -> check per-device-token failure limit and exempt user-only and IP keys, else check the deferred IP key and user-only key; 4) hash. Lets a previously used device of an attacked admin still log in.

Signed token {user id, issuing ver, HMAC(fp-key, normalized login name) fingerprint, random, 90-day expiry} with kid-addressed key set so rotation does not break it; no raw login name inside; valid only if the fingerprint matches this attempt's name and user id/ver equal the token; ver++ and password change invalidate it; per-device-token 5 failures per 15 min then invalidated (stored shared in JDBC mode, immediately in file mode); delivered by cookie naru_device or body deviceToken and header Naru-Device (header preferred over cookie on read).
Hard lock only when a Lockout policy is specified; not applied to trusted-device requests; applies to password login only (API key auth unaffected); released by DELETE /auth/admin/users/:id/lockout.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: LoginThrottle SPI with limit arguments and ForwardingLoginThrottle
requirement_inventory.notes: retryAfter(key)/recordFailure(key) plus default retryAfter(key,max,windowMillis)/recordFailure(key,max,windowMillis) delegating to the 1-arg versions and `default boolean usesLimitArguments()` (false by default, true for built-ins); ForwardingLoginThrottle abstract class forwards all of them together; API key enabled with usesLimitArguments false -> doctor WARN. Fixed before first release.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Throttle storage, memory cap and persistence
requirement_inventory.notes: In-memory counters capped (JVM 100,000 keys, Android 10,000) evicting oldest with one WARN; file store snapshots every 60 s, never per failure; JDBC store updates atomically (count = count + 1) so N nodes do not multiply limits; device-token invalidation is persisted immediately in file mode.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Per-user password attempt limit shared by password confirmations
requirement_inventory.notes: User-id keyed 15 min / 5 limit used by POST /auth/password, AuthUsers.checkPassword, POST /auth/me/apikeys and POST /auth/admin/apikeys; exceeding -> 429 (AuthRejection with retryAfterSeconds for app calls); success does not reset the counter; failures are not counted differently for unknown ids.

Framework value class (not annotations): id String, username, passwordHash (`transient`, Gson only, only for default-modifier Gson), ver, enabled, roles, attributes Map, isServiceAccount() immutable after creation; toBuilder(); no direct scopes in v1; getX/isX naming for Kotlin properties.

Five required synchronous `throws Exception` methods: findByUsername, findById, create, update, delete. Five default field methods: updatePasswordHash(id, expectedOldHash, newHash) boolean, boolean changePassword(id, expectedOldHash, expectedVer, newHash), setEnabled, bumpTokenVersion, setRoles. IDs are strings and deleted IDs are never reused; ver only increases.

Per-user lock -> re-read -> compare expectation -> update(row) -> re-read to confirm; unconfirmed security writes (setEnabled, bumpTokenVersion, setRoles) retry up to 3 times then 503 security_write_conflict + audit; only rehash is silently skipped; rehash compares passwordHash, ver, enabled, roles of the login-time copy with the re-read row; all auth-triggered user writes use fresh rows under this lock.

Store must implement all five field methods atomically and update() must not write passwordHash/ver/enabled/roles; declares true via `default boolean supportsAtomicFieldWrites()`; false under MULTI_INSTANCE -> doctor FAIL; no reflection in doctor.

expectedOldHash null equals null (SSO or legacy users without hash can receive passwords); self-service re-verifies current password against the re-read hash and retries once, otherwise 409; admin reset never retries (409); success response and token pair only after the write truly applied; JDBC form: UPDATE ... SET password_hash=?, ver=ver+1 WHERE id=? AND ver=? AND (password_hash=? OR (password_hash IS NULL AND ? IS NULL)).
Built-ins take one lock over the name index for check+write and throw DuplicateUserException on unique violation; file store persists with versioned format via AtomicFiles and MiniJson FILE profile.

Temp file -> FileDescriptor.sync() -> existing to .bak -> temp to main name -> delete .bak. On start: only .bak -> restore with WARN; main and .bak -> use main if readable and delete .bak; main unreadable -> FAIL and overwrite nothing. Directory fsync impossible on API 21 (documented limitation, ver may regress after power loss).

Public abstract class forwarding every UserStore method incl. defaults; the five field methods and the atomic declaration are forwarded to the delegate only when delegate.supportsAtomicFieldWrites() is true, else `UserStore.super.x(...)` so the decorator's own findById/update are used; Javadoc documents it; updated whenever UserStore gains a default method.

findById, findByUsername, create(name, char[] password, roles...), create(..., @Nullable UserMutator init, roles...), update(id, mutator), delete(id), rename(id, newName), checkPassword(id, char[]); all returned/passed AuthUser are passwordHash-stripped copies; throws only DuplicateUserException, AuthUnavailableException, IllegalArgumentException, AuthRejection; fires the same before/on events; original store via auth.userStore() (Javadoc warns: never feed stripped copies to its update).

Own @FunctionalInterface (java.util.function.Function is API 24+); applied inside the per-user lock to a freshly read row; changing passwordHash (non-null), ver, enabled, roles, id, username or serviceAccount -> IllegalArgumentException; stripped-hash comparison, original hash restored when writing.

Login identifier is an opaque String; auth only applies NFKC normalization and Locale.ROOT lower-casing before store.findByUsername; rename/A4 username change normalizes, duplicates -> DuplicateUserException (409), same-as-current is a no-op; old device tokens invalidated automatically by fingerprint mismatch. No email/phone login API; the store decides lookup and uniqueness.

Takes the hash slot, uses the user-id 5/15min limit (AuthRejection 429 with retryAfterSeconds), unknown id or null hash -> dummy hash then false (same timing), success does not reset the counter and never re-hashes, slot wait > 5 s -> AuthUnavailableException; caller wipes char[]; body passwords arrive as String and are converted (Gson cannot read char[]).
Unchecked, HTTP 409; stores throw it on unique-key violations in create/update and that is the final authority (auth's pre-check is just fast feedback); verified by verifyUserStore.

AuthTesting.verifyUserStore(store) checks CRUD, DuplicateUserException on unique violation, hash round trip (survives save and reload, relevant to the transient field), changePassword with null hash and ver mismatch, field-method atomics, and that update() does not overwrite security fields.

`ver++` once revokes access, refresh, device tokens, WebSocket and API keys: triggered by logout?all=true, password change, disable, recovery; role/group changes do NOT bump ver (reflected through the 5 s cache and the key decision formula); ver is monotonic (UserStore invariant, Javadoc). Passwords changes require reissuing API keys.

`resource:action` with [a-z0-9-]{1,32} each; wildcards only on the grant side: `resource:*` and `*`; `*` covers everything, `r:*` covers r:* and all r:a, `r:a` covers only itself; admin scopes auth-users, auth-groups, auth-apikeys x read/write (plus resource wildcards) only; any other auth-* resource reserved and rejected (RolePolicy.build() throws; RoleStore rows filtered with one WARN).

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Grant rule: only what you hold (R31 (1)-(3))
requirement_inventory.notes: Actor scopes A are re-read from the store (never the principal cache); (1) any newly gained scope (roles, groups, memberships, edges, API key scopes) must be covered by A; (2) modifying/resetting/disabling/deleting/removing from a target requires the target's current effective scopes covered by A; (3) no self change of roles/groups, no self disable/delete (also when the actor is among users affected by a group delete/edge removal); denials audited, 403 insufficient_scope. Built-in admin passes everything.

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: Reference DDL for SQLite, MySQL and PostgreSQL
requirement_inventory.notes: Reference schema per dialect for users (with serviceAccount column), groups, refresh tokens, throttle, device trust and API keys; naru_api_key_owner(owner_user_id PRIMARY KEY) lock table; unique prefix index with binary collation (MySQL utf8mb4_bin/ascii_bin); indexes (owner_user_id, expires_at, owner_ver) and (expires_at).

1) autocommit statement creating the lock row (MySQL INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE owner_user_id=owner_user_id; PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING); 2) open transaction (PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED; MySQL isolation unchanged; no START TRANSACTION WITH CONSISTENT SNAPSHOT and no plain read before step 3); 3) SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the lock row; 4) plain COUNT(*) of live keys; 5) insert if below the limit and commit, else rollback and false. Retries up to 3x with 10-100 ms random delay on 40001, 40P01, 55P03 and MySQL 1205 (with explicit rollback).

requirement_inventory.candidate_title: JdbcApiKeyStore session settings and connection hygiene
requirement_inventory.notes: Set innodb_lock_wait_timeout=5 / lock_timeout=5 s before step 1; capture and restore autocommit, isolation and lock-wait settings (and busy_timeout) in all outcomes before returning the connection; accept only a DataSource that hands out connections not enlisted in outer transactions (no Spring TransactionAwareDataSourceProxy, no JTA); Javadoc documents this because doctor cannot detect it.

Connection stays autocommit; execute BEGIN IMMEDIATE and COMMIT/ROLLBACK statements directly (no lock row needed); PRAGMA busy_timeout 5000 ms, SQLITE_BUSY -> store error -> 503; one in-process lock per normalized DB file path (strip `file:` prefix and `?` parameters, absolute path; memory DBs keyed by the whole connection string) making two instances in one process deterministic; case-insensitive filesystems may yield two locks (accepted).

Delete expired keys in batches of 500 per statement/transaction until fewer than 500 are removed; MySQL `DELETE ... ORDER BY expires_at, id LIMIT 500`, PostgreSQL/SQLite `DELETE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... LIMIT 500)`; Javadoc warns about MySQL warning 1592 under binlog_format=STATEMENT and recommends ROW or MIXED.
deleteFutureByOwner overridden as a single DELETE ... WHERE owner_user_id=? AND owner_ver>?; deleteStaleByOwner with owner_ver<?; both return deleted counts.

See ambiguity on test-scope drivers.

ambiguities.topic: Test-scope JDBC drivers vs 'no new dependencies'
ambiguities.detail: JDBC stores and the JdbcApiKeyStore locking procedure cannot be verified without a driver, while 00 forbids any new dependency; 00 section 12 admits MySQL/PostgreSQL behavior is unmeasured.
